diagnostics.detail: Reader-state JSON was exported only after shared verifier acceptance.
diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: A citizen reported in a video that the price of psychiatric drugs has increased by more than 300 percent compared to two months ago. He can afford his own medication but expressed concern for others. This report was published by Iran International.

A video shows that the grass at Azadi Stadium has been removed and tunnels are under renovation. The CEO of the Sports Facilities Development Company stated that construction will finish in October and initial operation will begin in December. Previously, the stadium was expected to be ready for the 1406–1405 season, but replacing the grass has delayed the preparation process.

The Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting has released a video that, according to this media, shows an American unmanned underwater vehicle. According to the report, the IRGC Navy "seized" this vessel near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz. On the other hand, a US official said that a military underwater vehicle of that country had a technical malfunction in the Middle East more than a day ago.

A group of women from the families of the disappeared lit candles in memory of protesters killed by the Islamic Republic. This event was shared on social media. They commemorated the memory of these protesters.

A citizen criticized the high prices of medicines in a video sent to Iran International. He asked what a low-income patient who urgently needs medicine should do. The video highlights concerns about access to medication.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said the presence of security, police, and Revolutionary Guard forces at some gas stations indicates the government's concern about repeating the November 2019 protests. He added that the Islamic Republic faces difficulties in continuing subsidies and raising fuel prices amid declining oil revenues and a fuel crisis.

The spokesperson of Khatam al-Anbia Headquarters condemned the US military threat to target three Iranian oil tankers. He stated that if Iranian ships are attacked, Iran's armed forces will target US bases and interests in the region. Iranian media also reported hearing explosions near Khark Island.

The German financial supervisory authority BaFin has declared the Bank Sepah branch in Frankfurt bankrupt. This branch can no longer repay deposits due to international sanctions. BaFin has activated the compensation process for depositors.

Mehdi Naseri and Aref Naseri, two citizens from Khuzestan, were arrested by the Intelligence Organization of the IRGC. Hossein Ahvazi and Mehdi Zaeri, two musicians, were summoned by the same security agency. The arrests are related to the production and release of the music piece "From Karun to Zaytun."

Donald Trump stated that tensions with the Islamic Republic will be resolved peacefully and the war will end soon. He also said that the Islamic Republic is likely responsible for the attack on the oil pipeline in Saudi Arabia. These remarks were made in response to a question about the attack.

Al-Nassr Saudi club unveiled its second kit for the new season with images of its Portuguese superstar, Cristiano Ronaldo. The club included a sarcastic caption aimed at Lionel Messi, stating: "The second; for the greatest history."

An overturned vehicle carrying seasonal workers on the Mirabad to Piranshahr route caused injuries to 16 workers. The incident occurred today in West Azerbaijan province. More details were published by Harana News Agency.

A citizen stated that despite having a doctor's prescription for restless leg syndrome, they are forced to obtain methadone. They were told to go to an addiction treatment clinic and register to buy the medicine. This highlights the drug crisis in the country.

Between July 11 and July 31, 2026, at least 72 social media pages and accounts in Iran were blocked or suspended, and 23 business units in various cities were sealed. These actions targeted bloggers, online businesses, cafes, sports clubs, and tour organizers. Similar measures were reported in Qazvin and Rasht.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, stated in an interview that Mojtaba Khamenei is alive and the US cannot locate him. He added that the US has targeted many leaders of the Islamic Republic. Pezeshkian made these remarks on Saturday, 21 Shahrivar.

Amir Ghalenoei has requested a monthly salary of 15 billion tomans to coach the national football team until the Asian Cup. This amount totals 90 billion tomans for six months. Fars News Agency has denied these reports, stating that no meeting about the salary has been held yet.
Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, met with Sheikh Khalid bin Mohammed Al Nahyan, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, on the sidelines of the BRICS summit.

Donald Trump stated that the war with the Islamic Republic will end after the US midterm elections in November. He added that oil prices will decrease after the conflict ends. He also mentioned that Houthi forces in Yemen have said they do not want the US to directly enter the conflict.

Gianni Infantino, FIFA president, announced his election slogan as "Football belongs to everyone, everywhere in the world." He confirmed he will run in the March 2027 election. This announcement comes amid at least 25 countries withdrawing their support from him.

Shayan Samiei said Trump currently prefers to observe the Yemen war from afar and avoid extensive involvement. If the Houthis cause serious disruption in energy transit, the US military may intervene. Trump is watching the Mecca Agreement to see what actions member countries will take.

CENTCOM announced that in the past 60 days, it has forced 100 commercial ships to change course. This action has taken place since the blockade of Iranian ports resumed. Additionally, no ship has passed through the blockade without US military authorization.

Two days after the attack on Saudi Arabia's most important oil pipeline, Trump said the attack was the work of the Islamic Republic. Simultaneously, the Houthis, Tehran-backed militias in Yemen, gained control of the Bab el-Mandeb strait by advancing.
Motorcycle couriers in Lahijan went on strike on Saturday, September 12, protesting their wages. They stopped working. This video was published by Iran International.

Esmaeil Baqaei stated that the IAEA and its director have issued ambiguous or incorrect reports used by the US and Israel to justify attacks on Iran. The Islamic Republic will pursue accountability of the agency and its director. Baqaei added that attacks against Iran began just one day after the IAEA report was published.

At the BRICS summit in New Delhi, the attending leaders each planted a sapling after taking a group photo. Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin were also present at the ceremony. The BRICS group approved a joint statement expressing deep concern about the war in the Middle East.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said closing border crossings is part of Baghdad's effort to control weapons and prevent the use of Iraqi territory against regional countries. He warned that if attacks from Iraq continue, controls and restrictions will increase. He also noted that Iraq could limit the transfer routes of equipment and forces to Iran and its allies.

Iran and Oman have reached a final agreement on new shipping routes. This agreement does not mean the Strait of Hormuz will be reopened; its reopening depends on the US meeting seven conditions set by Tehran. The new routes for entering and exiting the Persian Gulf will be under Iran's control.

Asieh Amini reported an increase in repression and arrests of citizens. She identified four simultaneous crises facing the Islamic Republic: legitimacy crisis, war and national security crisis, economic crisis, and the potential for another popular uprising. This situation has led to increased pressure and suppression of protests.

The TankerTrackers institute reported that Iran's oil production has decreased and is now roughly equal to domestic consumption and refining. Therefore, Iran will not face a shortage of oil storage space. The National Iranian Oil Company does not have significant problems storing surplus oil.
A citizen stated in a video that they paid 490,000 tomans for a melon and two kilograms of potatoes. This indicates a price increase for these products. The video was published by Iran International.

The G7 parliamentary meeting will start on Thursday in Paris. The heads of parliaments of G7 member countries, along with the presidents of the European and Ukrainian parliaments, will meet and discuss. This report is by Sajedeh Sharifi from Iran International.

Maryam Azimi Hashemi, a member of Apple's camera technology team, received her bachelor's degree from Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. She continued her master's and doctoral studies at the University of British Columbia. In 2023, Azimi introduced new portrait photography features for the iPhone 15.

A craftsman criticized the downturn of his industrial unit in a video published on social media. He said that in the past 47 years, the economic and business situation has never been this bad. This video reflects economic concerns.

A citizen stated in a video that they paid 1,100,000 tomans for several dairy products. He held the Islamic Republic responsible for this situation. This issue has raised concerns about rising prices.

Mehdi Tartaar, Persepolis coach, announced the unilateral cancellation of their match against Kheybar by the league organization without coordination. He stated that the club had not requested the cancellation and that the decision caused shock and dissatisfaction. Tartaar emphasized that his team opposes the cancellation and wants the match to be played.

One of the protesters injured by a bullet in December is still unable to walk. This person has undergone 23 surgeries and recovery of mobility may take at least another year. The treatment costs and security concerns have put significant pressure on him and his family.

The US has stated that it targeted 10 tankers linked to the Islamic Republic in the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman in three waves. Among these tankers, the sinking of two vessels named Kaylo and Risko has been confirmed.

The mother of Soda Akramifard, a protester killed in December 2025, joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." She urged others to light candles in memory of the eternal names. This video was shared on social media.

TankerTrackers reported that ship-to-ship transfers of crude oil in the Gulf of Oman reached 7.15 million barrels per day over the past 14 days, a 56 percent increase from the previous month. The increase comes amid ongoing concerns about shipping security in the Strait of Hormuz.

A sick citizen told Iran International in a video that the pharmacy official said the increase in gasoline prices caused the rise in drug prices. This issue was mentioned as the reason for the increased cost of medicine. This statement was made by the pharmacy official.

Military sources from the Yemeni government say that the Houthis, supported by the Islamic Republic, are trying to strengthen their position near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Reuters, citing four military sources, reported that the Houthis have nearly full control over coastal areas including the ports of Mocha and Dhubab. More details were provided by an Iran International reporter.

A protest rally was held in Rome in support of Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, two 19-year-old Iranian sisters sentenced to death and 25 years in prison. Representatives from the 'Moderates' party and other members of the Italian parliament called for an end to executions and torture of political prisoners in Iran. The main slogan of the rally was 'Freedom is not hanged.'

People report becoming angry more quickly and having less tolerance than before. The poor economic and social conditions have negatively affected people's mental health. Additionally, the price of Depakine, a medication for nerves, has significantly increased.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh stated that the Islamic Republic has deployed military and security forces in schools. This move is to use schools as a protective layer for their forces. There are also reports of attempts to permanently seize some schools.

The Iranian Football League Organization announced that four matches of the seventh week of the Premier League have been postponed due to the presence of players in the national youth team camp. The matches Zob Ahan - Sepahan, Kheybar - Persepolis, Malavan - Foolad, and Fajr Sepasi - Aluminium will not be held. The new dates for these matches will be announced later.

The father of Amirhossein Sheikhbu, a protester killed in December 2025, joined the "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" campaign by visiting his son's grave. He said each candle reminds of thousands of lives, names, memories, and absences.

Pakistan has sent a message to Tehran asking the Islamic Republic to control the Houthis. On Tuesday, the Houthis attacked a Saudi Arabian airbase and oil infrastructure. These attacks injured 73 people.

After missile launches by the IRGC at US bases in Jordan and interception of some in Israeli airspace, the Israeli army has raised its alert level. Benjamin Netanyahu and Yisrael Katz warned that Israel will not allow the reconstruction of Iran's missile and nuclear capabilities. An interview was conducted with Babak Es-haqi, a journalist from Iran International.

The National Resistance media in Yemen announced that it obtained maps showing the IRGC's plan for advancing and controlling the Bab al-Mandab Strait. These maps were found on the laptop of a captured Houthi commander. The images show four stages of advancement towards the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the city of Hodeidah.

The mother of Ali Ghorbani Toraghi, a protester killed in December 2025, honored her son's memory by joining the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." She said, "I neither forgive nor forget." This video was published on social media.

Maryam Azimi, an Iranian Apple engineer, introduced the "Apple Reference Image" technology at the global unveiling of the iPhone 18 Pro. This technology enables verification of photo authenticity and detection of edited or AI-generated images. Her presence attracted attention due to her role in technology development and her public stance against the Islamic Republic.

Hamidreza Omidi, CEO of the Hijab Activists Association, stated that the price of black chadors is highly dependent on the dollar rate. He added that producers have lost about 10% of their capital in the past 48 hours. Selling the product is not profitable for them.

Ali Parvin commented on Khodadad Azizi's audio file, saying Khodadad should be careful and hopes the issue will be resolved. He also said that Persepolis started the league well and has had an acceptable performance so far. Parvin believes if the team continues this way, they will become champions.

Asal Mansouri was killed by Khamenei's forces with live ammunition during the protests on January 9 in Tehran. This event remains in the memory of the Iranian people. Her memory will be preserved as a guiding light for freedom seekers.

The mother of Maedeh Moradi Kian lit a candle on her daughter's grave and said she will live until she avenges her. Maedeh Moradi Kian, 22 years old, was killed by gunfire from officers on January 9 in Qaemshahr. This video was published on social media.

Babak Negahdari, head of the Parliament Research Center, stated that public preference for ceasefire and negotiation dropped from 60% between May and July to 45% between July and September. The inclination towards confrontation and preemptive attack on the US increased by 10 percentage points. Details of the survey method and participant numbers were not disclosed.

Mohammad Şimşek, Turkey's Minister of Finance, stated that Ankara has taken note of the recent US sanctions related to economic activities with Iran. He emphasized that Turkish companies and financial institutions must fully comply with domestic laws. These remarks were made in an interview with Narges Horkhsh.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said Trump's remarks about 'Kuh-e Kalanq' indicate that Washington believes the Islamic Republic is rebuilding part of its nuclear capacity. He added that moving activities underground does not protect them from military pressure.

The sister of Ahmad Khosravani posted a video expressing her pain and longing eight months after his death. Ahmad Khosravani, a student at Sharif University of Technology and a basketball player, was shot dead on the evening of January 8, 2026. He was the champion of the Tehran 3x3 basketball tournament and the best player in the Tehran league in 2025.

Hossein Akbari, deputy of natural environment at Isfahan Environmental Protection, attributed the mass death of fish in the Zayandeh Rud riverbed to the water flow cut. He stated that the regional water company must take responsibility for this incident. After the water flow was cut on September 6, thousands of fish died and some were trapped in remaining pools.

A 35-year-old person stated that due to difficult economic conditions and life pressures, they get angry faster than before, and society has become very angry and hostile. They mentioned an increase in conflicts and a decrease in people's tolerance. This situation has caused depression and psychological pressure among the people.
Mohammad Amin Salami's brother commemorated his brother and other martyrs by lighting a candle. He said their names will remain immortal throughout history.

The Islamic Republic of Iran has used a barter-like mechanism to bypass oil sanctions and purchase goods from China. This mechanism has been active since 2021 and was initially used to procure medicine and COVID-19 vaccines. It has also been used to buy cars, communication equipment, and air defense systems.

Mohammad Qaedi, an international relations lecturer, said Pakistan is mediating between Saudi Arabia and the Islamic Republic. Saudi Arabia still prefers diplomacy over military confrontation. However, continued Houthi attacks and heavy casualties may force Saudi Arabia to react.

A report on the economic difficulties faced by people in Iran, including reduced wages, rising prices of goods and services, and issues caused by power outages and financial restrictions. A threefold increase in electricity bills in Tehran and educational problems in Khorramabad were also mentioned. These conditions have led to depression and dissatisfaction among the people.

Mohammad Sadegh Motamedian, the governor of Tehran, called for the return of schools that have been taken over by other organizations. He emphasized that these educational spaces must be returned to the Ministry of Education before the start of the school year. The governor did not specify which organizations are involved.

The Iranian national basketball team lost 59-53 to Qatar in their first game at the Nagoya Asian Games. The first quarter ended tied at 10-10, and Qatar led 31-21 at halftime. Iran will next face Taiwan and Jordan in the group stage.

Lamine Yamal became the youngest captain in Barcelona's history at 19 years and 58 days old. He received the captain's armband from Rafinha during the match against Feyenoord and scored six minutes later. The previous record was held by Bojan Krkic, who became captain at 20 years and 56 days old.

Roghayeh Rezaei reported an increase in the prices of menstrual hygiene products. She stated that the Islamic Republic imposes restrictions on women's bodies alongside pro-natalist policies. Additionally, necessary support for women's healthcare is not provided.

The "Jan Faday Iran" exercise will be held on September 17 with the participation of Basij forces, the Revolutionary Guards, and police. The commander of Tehran's Revolutionary Guards stated that this exercise demonstrates the readiness and determination of the Iranian nation. Its purpose is declared to confront the enemies.

Marzieh Hosseini, a reporter for Iran International, has reported on Donald Trump's speech at the Republican gathering. She mentioned the possibility of another US attack on the Kooh Kalang facilities. She also examined the connection between the war with the Islamic Republic and the US midterm elections.

Sahar Khodayari, an Esteghlal fan, self-immolated in protest against a six-month prison sentence for attempting to enter Azadi Stadium and died on September 9, 2019. She had been accused of various charges including public indecency. Her death received widespread international attention.

Shahram Kholdi referred to Donald Trump's statements about the attack on the Kuh-e-Kalang facility and said that if the attack does not lead to the complete destruction of the facility, the Islamic Republic will move towards militarizing its nuclear program.

Shayan Samiei said Trump has left the door open for negotiations with the Islamic Republic but considers the previous agreement ended. He added that Trump sends a message to the Iranian people that they are separate from the government.

Donald Trump warned the Islamic Republic about activities at Kuh-e Kalanq Gezla and said Iran should not have nuclear weapons. He emphasized that Iran cannot have nuclear weapons and criticized past efforts to negotiate with Iran. Trump also mentioned the possibility of targeting these facilities.

Donald Trump stated that the decision to attack Iran's nuclear facilities was made after receiving reports about Tehran's proximity to nuclear weapons. He said some officials wanted to delay the attack, but he opposed it. Trump also discussed the bomber operation and the possibility of attacking Kuh-e Kolang Gazla.

Donald Trump said at a Republican gathering in Dallas that the war with the Islamic Republic will end shortly after the November 3 midterm elections. He added that Tehran wants a deal with the Democrats.

Reuters, citing a CBS reporter, reported that several US military aircraft were damaged in nighttime attacks on the Al-Salti airbase in Jordan. An A-10 Thunderbolt lost one of its wings, and about eight F-15s sustained minor damage but returned to service. The Islamic Republic announced that it had targeted the base with ballistic missiles.

The Saudi-led coalition announced that the Houthis targeted the cities of Khamis Mushait, Abha, and Jazan with ballistic missiles and drones on Wednesday, September 8. The coalition spokesperson stated that their response to these attacks will be within the framework of the right to self-defense. Additionally, Saudi Arabia has asked Iran through Pakistan to influence the Houthis to stop the attacks, but Tehran said it does not control the Houthis.

The Wall Street Journal, quoting American officials, reported that senior White House advisors have discussed with President Donald Trump the possibility of the war with the Islamic Republic continuing until the end of his presidency and even beyond January 2029. According to the report, JD Vance, the US Vice President, Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, and other officials discussed the possibility of Tehran continuing its resistance against military siege and pressures. This assessment differs from Trump's public statements, where he said the war would end "immediately" after the November midterm elections.

The Islamic Republic used missiles equipped with electro-optical guidance systems for the first time in attacks on US warships on Wednesday, September 8. CENTCOM confirmed the missile attacks but stated that no ships were hit. The Revolutionary Guards claimed to have targeted two American vessels and several tankers and ships.

The Transitional Justice Committee, chaired by Shirin Ebadi, warned the commanders and executors of protesters' executions that each of them will be held accountable. The committee stated that no leniency will be shown and all legal tools will be used for prosecution and punishment. It also emphasized that each execution increases criminal responsibility and these crimes will not be forgotten.

The Center for Strategic and International Studies reported that satellite images show increased construction activities in the underground complex of Kuh-e Kalang Gazla near the Natanz nuclear facility in 2026. Activities have shifted from excavation to internal construction and tunnel entrance reinforcement. The center neither confirmed nor denied claims of centrifuge transfers to this complex.

Hadad Adel stated that the Islamic Republic has failed regarding women's dress code. He said policies that ignore women's right to choose have caused this failure. He also emphasized that people have not been influenced by enemy infiltration but have moved beyond the government's policies.

Hadad Adel said that the Islamic Republic's work on women's dress has become more difficult and that the enemy promotes a Western lifestyle. He mentioned the failure of policies that do not recognize women as having the right to choose. This topic is discussed in a program hosted by Kambiz Hosseini.

The Iranian Transitional Justice Committee warned the perpetrators and commanders of protester executions that these crimes will be pursued without leniency. Afshin Elyan emphasized the need to document executions and human rights violations, stating those involved will face legal responsibility. He urged citizens to securely keep documents related to executions for use in transitional justice and international legal proceedings.

Arash Aramesh, a lawyer and security expert, said the Trump administration has not yet made a final decision on its ultimate strategy towards the Islamic Republic. He added that the US is currently between three options: escalating the war, continuing the status quo, or moving towards a deal, and it is not yet clear which path it will choose. He also said the US has the military capability to conduct limited ground operations, including on some strategic Iranian islands, but the decision depends more on political will than military factors.

Reuters reported that Iran has obtained a US Navy underwater drone. The drone, an older Dive-LD model, was found by Iranian forces after a technical failure. Iran may reverse-engineer parts of the drone, but this is unlikely to provide a decisive military advantage for Tehran.

Chris Wright, the US Energy Secretary, announced that more contracts with oil companies in Venezuela will be announced soon. He previously said these contracts would more than double Venezuela's oil production. Increased investment in Venezuela's energy sector could significantly boost oil production capacity.

Hossein Mohebbi, spokesperson for the IRGC, dismissed Benjamin Netanyahu's threats and considered Israel too small to carry out threats against Iran. Netanyahu had stated that Israel is ready to act against Iran if necessary. He also said that they must finish what they started with the Islamic Republic.

The defense company Covenant, supported by Peter Thiel, has started producing long-range, low-cost cruise missiles. The company designed the 'Anthem' missile with heavy payload capacity and has conducted about 200 test flights. Covenant has received orders worth $150 million, with deliveries starting in 2027.

Railway workers protested in front of the Ministry of Roads and Urban Development in Tehran. They protested against repression and poor living conditions, chanting slogans against the minister. They threatened to strike if their problems were not resolved.

A program with Kambiz Hosseini about unprecedented sanctions on Iranian aviation has been released. The program discusses the possibility of all flights being canceled. The main topic is the sanctions and their impact on Iran's flights.

Palmer Luckey, founder of Anduril, stated that the Dive-DL drone is designed so that losing it in operations does not create a security problem. The drone is made for extremely dangerous environments and its loss is acceptable. He added that the device provided significant operational value for months before falling into enemy hands.

Ali Tajernia, chairman of Esteghlal club, used the Lion and Sun flag in a post on X, which was later removed and replaced with the Islamic Republic flag. This change coincided with the Iranian National Revolution in December 2025 and followed a user's request on X. Tajernia had previously commemorated the founder of the Taj club.

Several explosions were heard in the coastal areas of Qeshm, Sirik, and Minab in the early hours of Thursday, September 19. The Hormozgan governorate stated that the sounds came from the sea, and no reports about the cause or damage have been released yet. The explosions were strong enough to shake buildings and windows.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry, denied Marco Rubio's claims that the Houthis are proxies of Iran, stating that the Houthis are an independent actor who take their own decisions. This response came after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia that injured at least 73 people. It was also reported that Saudi Arabia sent a message through Pakistan asking Iran to intervene to stop the Houthi attacks.

Rouhollah Najabat stated that the Islamic Republic will accelerate the technical development of its nuclear program in response to the IAEA Board of Governors resolution. He emphasized that Iran will not give any concessions and will respond more firmly. Najabat also described the resolution as political and held Western countries responsible for any potential tensions.

The Yemeni Armed Forces Media Center released a video showing clashes between Saudi-backed government forces and Houthi forces near Al Hazm. These clashes have intensified in recent months, raising concerns about a return to a broader war. Yemeni government forces have launched a multi-front attack to reclaim areas controlled by the Houthis.

The Yemeni Armed Forces Media Center released a video showing clashes between Saudi-backed government forces and Houthi forces. The exact time and location of the video recording have not been confirmed. Clashes have intensified recently, and Yemeni government forces have launched a multi-front attack on Houthi-controlled areas.

Alireza Salimi stated that leaving the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) could be one of Iran's options to respond to the IAEA Board of Governors resolution. He described the resolution as political and hostile and said Iran has not benefited from the treaty's rights. Salimi predicted that actions related to the resolution would face a veto due to Russia and China's membership in the Security Council.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, said that the Islamic Republic has not received assistance to change the war conditions. He added that the Islamic Republic attacks US Navy ships but has lost five of its oil tankers in response. Rubio emphasized that the US will continue to economically suffocate the Islamic Republic.

The mother of Setareh Rafiei lit a candle in the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" in memory of her daughter. Setareh Rafiei, 19 years old, was killed on January 9, 2026, in Narmak, Tehran. Her mother stated that she neither forgives nor forgets.

The head of the Iranian Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Association warned about a 59% increase in liver cancer over the past 10 years. Shahram Kordasti attributed this rise to poor nutrition, fatty liver, and weak prevention programs. He emphasized the importance of prevention and the challenges in accessing medical services.

Al Nassr football team defeated Abha 2-1 in the sixth week of the Saudi Professional League. Cristiano Ronaldo scored the first goal in the 22nd minute, bringing his career goal tally to 979. With this win, Al Nassr achieved their fifth victory and tied in points with Al Hilal and Al Qadsiah.

A citizen installed a street sign named Mahsa Amini Street in eastern Seyyed Ghotb Street, Piranshahr, on the eve of the anniversary of Mahsa Zeina Amini's death. This act is shown in a video received by Iran International.

Farzin Nadimi stated that conventional bombs may not be sufficient to completely destroy the underground facilities of Kuh-e Kalang-Gazla. The Pentagon is considering developing more advanced penetrator weapons and new operational scenarios. Additionally, locations near the Strait of Hormuz hold greater military significance than Khark Island.

Meir Javdanfar said there are signs of increasing disagreement between Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu. Their relations remain good, but Trump's stance on the upcoming Israeli elections is important. Among Trump's advisors, there is also disagreement on how to deal with Netanyahu.

A citizen stated in a video that last year he started a business by selling his gold but has not recovered his initial capital until now. He shared this issue on social media. This complaint points to financial problems in the business.

Pakistan has conveyed Saudi Arabia's message to Tehran, asking Iran to use its influence to stop Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Tehran responded that it does not control the Houthis. Sources also said that last week Tehran asked the Houthis to attack Saudi Arabia and promised financial and military support.

Sardar Azmoun has been re-invited to the Iranian national football team after recent controversies and government criticisms. He is expected to participate in the upcoming FIFA international window and preparations for the Asian Cup. This return comes after Azmoun distanced himself from the national team and had his assets seized.

A video from the evening of September 8 shows that a government gathering in one of the squares in Qom was sparse. The seats at this gathering were mostly empty. This video was received by Iran International.

Donald Trump stated that the war with Iran will end immediately after the 2026 US elections. He said he is no longer seeking an agreement with the Islamic Republic and that negotiations might occur but are not the current focus. Trump also mentioned working on matters beyond the nuclear deal, involving new issues.

A citizen says they have to buy various medicines every month but the prices have become very expensive. They are worried they might not be able to afford their medicines anymore. They also attribute the rise in medicine prices to the increase in gasoline prices.

Ismail Baqaei, the Foreign Ministry spokesperson, said that referring Iran's nuclear case to the UN Security Council is irrelevant because Iran has not violated any commitments. He attributed the issues raised in the Board of Governors resolution to attacks by the US and Israel. Baqaei described Japan and Saudi Arabia's positive vote on the resolution as ineffective.

Mohammed bin Zayed, the UAE president, warned Netanyahu about Yahya Sinwar's plan to attack Israel one week before October 7. Netanyahu denied the warning and said no such call took place. UAE officials neither confirmed nor denied the report.

An informed source told Iran International that the health and humanitarian situation in Qom Central Prison is dire. Most prisoners have contracted influenza and COVID-19. The prison environment is heavily contaminated and the prisoners' daily food rations are insufficient.

A US official told NewsNation that American forces are not conducting any attacks near Jask, following reports of an explosion sound. The Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting had reported hearing an explosion from the direction of the Strait of Hormuz in Jask on Wednesday evening.

Alireza Ardoubadi resigned from the Persepolis club board. Hossein Saberi was introduced as the new member and chairman of the board. Ardoubadi left Persepolis due to his candidacy for the Bank Shahr board.

A video has been released showing a young woman singing a local song at the grave of Omid Sarlak. She pays respect in front of his picture installed at the grave. Omid Sarlak, a 27-year-old athlete from Aligudarz, was suspiciously killed in November 2025.

Eight months after the killing of protesters in January 2026, images of body bags that families search through to find their loved ones remain in the collective memory of Iranians. These bags have become a symbol of death and repression in recent protests. Previously, such images were mostly seen in cinema and natural disasters.

Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel will not allow any terrorist army to be stationed on its borders. He called the Islamic Republic a terrorist regime and said Israel's main goal is to defeat the Iranian government. Netanyahu also mentioned Israel's unprecedented control over the region.

The US Central Command announced that American forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers. CENTCOM denied the IRGC's claim of targeting two American warships. The Saudi foreign minister warned about the consequences of Houthi attacks.

An electronics specialist and industrial board repair technician stated that he has not found work for several years and his life situation is disrupted. This was reported in a video to Iran International. He is experiencing difficult circumstances.

Fars news agency reported hearing an explosion sound on Wednesday evening in Jask. The sound was heard from the sea in the southern areas of Jask county. The source of this news is Fars, affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards.

The Israeli Prime Minister said Israel will not allow any terrorist army to be stationed on its borders during a visit to the army positions on Mount Hermon. He called the Islamic Republic a terrorist regime and stated that Israel's main goal is to defeat the Iranian government. Netanyahu added that they are close to achieving this goal.

Saeed Javanmard, a former army officer, has been sentenced to a total of eight years in prison in two judicial cases. He was expelled from the army and sentenced to three years in prison after participating in the 1401 protests. In a new case, he was sentenced to five years for charges including cooperation with hostile states and disrupting order.

Reza Najafi stated that with the end of the war, verification activities by the agency in Iran will be possible. He said the comprehensive safeguards agreement does not have specific regulations for wartime conditions. He also emphasized that military attacks by the US and Israel have affected the implementation of safeguards in Iran.

The United States has sanctioned 27 companies and entities related to Iranian aviation and suspended three general licenses in this sector. The stated goal of these sanctions is to increase pressure on the Islamic Republic. This decision may affect travel for medical treatment, education, work, and family visits.

Ali Tajernia, acting CEO of Esteghlal club, stated that the club is requesting the championship trophy for the unfinished season. He emphasized that Esteghlal was in the best position when the league stopped and that the request is being made legally through correspondence. He also mentioned that if they wanted to cause trouble, they would have already obtained the trophy.

The US military launched a nighttime attack targeting five Iranian oil tankers, destroying about 12% of Iran's tanker fleet within a week. The spokesperson of the Revolutionary Guards presented six new conditions from the Islamic Republic to end the war. Acceptance of these conditions by Trump was emphasized.

The Panama-flagged tanker New Andros was targeted by a drone attack in Iraqi waters and caught fire. The tanker was carrying about two million barrels of fuel oil. No casualties were reported among the 22 crew members.

A video has been released showing the Shomrud River flooding in the Malfajan rural district of Siahkal county. This incident occurred in the Malfajan rural district. Reports indicate the river has overflowed.

A citizen criticized the high price of injectable insulin pens in a video sent to Iran International. He highlighted the economic pressure on patients who cannot afford the medication. He blamed the Islamic Republic for this situation.

Donald Trump has sent a message to Tehran through Pakistani and Qatari officials that he will not return to the previous agreement between Tehran and Washington. The Pakistani army commander and Qatari delegations conveyed this message to the Islamic Republic officials. The Islamic Republic stated that it only accepts the existing agreement and is not willing to make another deal.

Mehdi Nakhl Ahmadi said the Islamic Republic wants to silence society's voice and political prisoners. He referred to Hossein Shanbehzadeh's message, who is imprisoned for placing a dot under Ali Khamenei's message. Nakhl Ahmadi also mentioned Fa'ezeh Hashemi's distortion of reality about prison.

Two weeks before the new school year begins, officials of the Islamic Republic have commented on stricter enforcement of mandatory hijab in educational centers. Gholamali Haddad Adel said that the current war conditions prevent serious engagement with the hijab issue. This topic was evaluated by Asieh Amini, a social issues analyst.

A number of Iranians gathered on Tuesday, 17 Shahrivar, in the central square of Hamburg. They protested against inflation and executions in Iran. The protesters demanded the release of political prisoners.

Benjamin Netanyahu stated during his visit to Mount Hermon that the main task is to defeat the terrorist regime of Iran and that Israel is very close to this goal. He emphasized that Israel will not allow any terrorist army to be stationed on its borders. Netanyahu also declared that Israel controls the entire area from Mount Hermon to the Mediterranean.

The spokesperson of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced the restricted area of the Islamic Republic from around Chabahar to parts of the Oman Sea and Arabian Sea. Vessels entering this area without coordination will be placed on the sanctions list. They will also be denied passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

Snapbox drivers in Semnan stopped working in protest against low fares, fuel costs, and commission rates. They announced that none of the drivers are currently working. This protest was seen in a video published on social media.

South Korea has entered a new phase of considering various options, including possible military participation against the Islamic Republic. Japan is focusing on diplomatic channels and direct talks with the Islamic Republic. These movements coincide with rising tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

The US Department of Defense is considering scenarios for rapid amphibious operations by Marines on uninhabited Iranian islands near the Strait of Hormuz. The goal is to turn these islands into surveillance and logistical bases to protect commercial ships. The USS Tripoli, with 3,500 Marines, is present in the area, and F-35B fighters will provide air support.

On Tuesday night, with increased security measures, several government motorcycle forces were deployed in the streets of Mashhad. This was shown in a video received by Iran International. The action was taken in response to security conditions.

Ali Tajernia explained that if the transfer window does not open, the two players will stay with Aluminium until mid-season and then return to Esteghlal. Esteghlal has fulfilled its financial commitments and provided the players to Aluminium without cost. He also emphasized the importance of loyalty to commitments in football.

The Hercules Star oil tanker near Dubai experienced an incident resulting in one crew member killed and another missing. The chartering company stated that a specialized team is searching for the missing crew, and other crew members are safe. Initial assessments indicate a possible drone attack on the tanker.
A video posted on social media shows a citizen visiting the Tomb of the Immortals. The person placed flowers on their gravestone. This event has been reflected in the virtual space.

The case of 18 prisoners in Dastgerd prison in Isfahan has been referred to the Revolutionary Court. They are accused of involvement in unrest and arson at the prison. They face the risk of receiving death sentences.

Mohammad Ali Ghadousi, head of the legal department of the Football Federation, stated that managers have not yet received official notification about the indictment. The case concerns a $20,000 bonus paid to board members after qualifying for the 2022 World Cup. Yashar Soltani also reported that indictments have been issued against several senior federation managers on embezzlement charges.

A citizen stated in a video that barrels containing gasoline or oil are being transported from Mahshahr refinery to Nakja Abad by trailer. This has happened recently. No further details have been provided.
A citizen reported paying 653,000 tomans for a roll of tape and a pack of labels. This was reported via a video to Iran International. The prices of these items have significantly increased.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center announced that a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile 28 nautical miles southeast of Iraq's Faw port. The tanker crew are safe and no environmental consequences have been reported so far. Authorities are investigating the incident and have urged vessels to exercise caution.

A citizen sarcastically commented in a video sent to Iran International that they are happy there is no electricity and the house is dark. He added that if they are not happy, they will be executed. This statement refers to the power outage situation.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry stated that the armed forces will respond decisively to any US aggression. This statement was issued after the US attacked several Iranian oil tankers on September 7. The ministry called these attacks a violation of international law and urged the UN Security Council to take action.

Soda Ebrahimi Shamsabadi, a 33-year-old blogger from Bandar Abbas, faces the death penalty. She was sentenced after months of detention and torture due to her media activities. Reza Pahlavi's communications office has called for international pressure to prevent the execution.

The Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs strongly condemned the recent Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia. Ankara warned about the threat to civilians and called for an immediate halt to the Houthis' aggressive actions. These attacks have escalated regional tensions and undermined diplomatic efforts to end the conflict in Yemen.

Two citizens commemorated the memory of the deceased in the December 2025 protests by lighting candles for Masoud Zatparvar and Esmail Beigi Harchgani. This was done by sending videos to Iran International. These individuals are recognized as martyrs.

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh, head coach of Esteghlal, stated before the match against Paykan that his team aims to win three points. He mentioned the players' fatigue due to recent travels and the need to manage their energy. He also commented on the attack line and the presence of players in the youth team.

Ebrahim Rezaei stated that Iran's membership in the NPT treaty has brought no benefit and sensitive information has been exposed to espionage. He criticized the IAEA for not aiding Iran's nuclear technology and called its director a Western agent. The Islamic Republic will respond to any possible IAEA Board of Governors resolution.

A member of Iran International's editorial team referred to the Pakistani defense minister's remarks about the possible activation of the Makkah defense pact. He said the military readiness of Turkey and Pakistan to defend Saudi Arabia and the global reactions against the Houthis indicate a major decision to close the proxy conflict in Yemen.

The official funeral ceremony of Harald V, the former king of Norway, was held today in Oslo. Members of royal families and high-ranking officials from various countries attended the ceremony. Tens of thousands are expected to be present along the procession route and in central Oslo.

A member of Iran International's editorial team referred to Pakistan's defense minister's remarks about the possible activation of the Makkah defense pact. Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia are ready to support Riyadh in the war against the Houthis if the current situation in the region continues. Additionally, the recapture of Sanaa and securing the Bab al-Mandab Strait have become priorities.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported an attack on a vessel 24 miles northwest of Rashid Port, Dubai. The tanker captain observed the vessel leaning, possibly due to water ingress after an unknown projectile hit. Authorities are investigating and have urged vessels to exercise caution and report suspicious activity.

Gholamali Haddad Adel stated that due to wartime conditions, the government cannot fully address the issue of hijab at the moment. He added that the influence of promoting Western lifestyle in schools is evident. He also mentioned that dealing with this issue is now more difficult than in the 1980s.

Jane Lawson has launched the "Golestan" project to create a global reference for Iranian performing arts from 1880 to 1980. This digital archive includes solo performances, plays, radio programs, and other related works. The materials are indexed and searchable by relevant keywords.
Videos sent by citizens to Iran International show a missile passing over the skies of Abhar and Khomein in the early morning of September 8.

Brent crude oil price reached 100 dollars per barrel for the first time since early August. This price increase occurred amid ongoing conflicts in the Persian Gulf. The US announced it destroyed five oil tankers linked to the Revolutionary Guard after unsuccessful missile attacks by Iran.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, addressed the US Secretary of Defense on September 8 via a Telegram post. He stated that the next target is the US energy assets in the region. This message was shared on social media.

The Islamic Republic launched a missile attack on Jordan. This attack has increased concerns about the expansion of conflict in the region. Tehran's target was a base used by American forces in Jordan.

Leila Morvati stated that China's influence over Iran and its role in purchasing oil could enable Beijing to affect Tehran. China has announced its readiness to mediate between Iran and the United States. However, it is unclear whether the US and hardline groups in Iran will accept Beijing's mediation.

Citizens reported the simultaneous passage of several missiles over the skies of Shahin Shahr, Najafabad, Khomeinishahr, and Baharestan. The number of missiles was reported to be between 4 and 9. The launch sites were identified as two military bases in Najafabad.

Ben Shelton defeated Carlos Alcaraz in the US Open quarterfinals to advance to the semifinals. The five-set match ended with scores of 6-7, 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, and 7-6 in favor of Shelton. Shelton will face Frances Tiafoe in the semifinals.

Pakistan has expressed its support for Saudi Arabia's right to defend its territory and citizens. The Pakistani Ministry of Foreign Affairs considers this right legitimate. This statement continues Pakistan's regional support for Saudi Arabia against proxy attacks by the Islamic Republic.

Ahmad Alavi, an economist, reported the intensification of the drug and treatment crisis in Iran. He identified the insurance budget deficit as a cause of the government's financial crisis and resource allocation issues. Financial pressure on pharmacies has led to direct treatment costs being passed to patients and the expansion of the drug black market.

Iraqi security forces discovered drone launch platforms in the Al-Tayeb area of Maysan province. These platforms were found after an attack on Saudi Arabia's oil pipeline, and the border area has been closed. The Iraqi Prime Minister agreed to Iran's request for joint investigations regarding these platforms.

Ruhollah Rahimpour stated that the CENTCOM strategic operation indicates the US is seeking to increase economic pressure on the Islamic Republic. He added that targeting Iranian oil tankers could directly pressure Iran's oil exports and foreign currency revenues.

Lionel Messi has reached a preliminary agreement with the owners of the Spanish club Eldense to purchase the team. Eldense recently promoted to La Liga 2, and Messi intends to acquire 100% of its shares without third-party involvement. Finalizing the deal requires approval from the Spanish High Sports Council.

A citizen in a video shared on social media criticized the economic and social situation and expressed concern about the future of children in Iran. He addressed those responsible for the current situation, saying they have suffered and are worried about the children's future. This video has gained attention on social media.

Kamran Ghazanfari, a Tehran representative, said we are practically on the brink of World War III due to international tensions. He assessed the likelihood of the US using nuclear weapons against Iran as very low. He also mentioned that the plan for Iran to exit the NPT treaty might be reconsidered in parliament.

An audio file reveals that a US military aircraft warned three Iranian oil tankers that their engine rooms would be targeted for violating a military blockade. The crew was asked to leave the engine rooms within 10 minutes. US forces targeted five oil tankers linked to the IRGC.

Raf Chikoni, head of the Australian parliamentary security committee, condemned the threats by the Islamic Republic's armed forces spokesperson against Persian-language media. He emphasized the right of journalists to work freely. Expelling the Iranian ambassador and sanctioning government agents were mentioned as possible Australian responses.

People from various cities in Iran have reported economic problems and drug shortages. Medical and pharmaceutical costs have increased, and some vital medicines are unavailable. There are also significant increases in prices and living expenses, especially electricity bills and car repairs.

The US, UK, France, and Germany submitted a draft resolution against the Islamic Republic to the IAEA Board of Governors. The resolution calls for referring Iran's nuclear case to the UN Security Council. This action is due to Tehran's failure to comply with nuclear non-proliferation commitments.

The Washington Post reported that Persian Gulf countries are strengthening their defense capabilities and creating alternative routes to reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing US-Iran war. Officials from the UAE and Qatar have stated that reliance on US security support is insufficient and regional countries must build more independent defense capabilities.

Abdolhossein Khosropanah, Secretary of the Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution, stated that there is a lack of hijab observance in some government offices and pharmacies. He emphasized that all executive bodies are required to monitor compliance with hijab regulations. He also mentioned that the council does not see a need for new regulations on chastity and hijab.

The US has sanctioned 27 Iranian airlines and foreign companies linked to Mahan Air. These sanctions target the transfer of personnel, sensitive equipment, and financial resources of the Islamic Republic. Additionally, the suspension of aviation licenses and maritime pressures create new restrictions on Tehran's external communications.

Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, described the Houthis as Iran's proxy forces and stated that Washington is closely monitoring the group's activities and the Islamic Republic's role in regional affairs.

Alireza Salimi, a member of the parliament's presidium, stated that the way to confront Israel is through resistance and a strong response. He criticized the Lebanese government's approach towards Israel, calling it a black mark on its political record. Salimi also emphasized that the Islamic Republic has always supported the resistance and will continue to do so.

Sadegh Beigdeli stated that the sanctions on 27 Iranian airlines and the network related to Mahan Air make the transfer of sensitive equipment, financial resources, and personnel by the Islamic Republic more difficult and costly. He added that simultaneous pressure on air and sea routes forces Tehran to use land routes more extensively. These routes are slower, more expensive, and have limited capacity.

Erfan Ghaneifard, a Middle East analyst, told Iran International that US intelligence and security cooperation with regional countries has entered a broad phase. He also believes that the expansion of the war by Tehran could lead to the formation of a regional coalition against the Islamic Republic.

The US Treasury Department announced that the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has sanctioned 27 Iranian airlines and seven aviation-related companies. Among the sanctioned entities are Ata, Chabahar, Iran Airtour, Aseman, Kish, Karun, Qeshm, Sepehran, Taban, Zagros, Varesh, and Fly Persia.

Mohammad Saleh Jokar warned that if the US continues the naval blockade, it will face a devastating response. He stated that US missile systems can no longer track Iranian missiles. Additionally, Iran's military and missile capabilities have significantly improved compared to the past.

Jacob Coxon, a 27-year-old researcher at Anthropic, is leaving the AI industry due to concerns about competition among tech companies to develop self-improving AI models. He warned that competition between American and Chinese companies could lead to compromises in safety. Over a thousand AI researchers have called for global coordination to slow down the development of self-improving models.

The family of Niloufar Majavari, who died last week following torture and assault, gathered at her grave in Zargatan Cemetery, Piranshahr, to condemn her murder. The suspect is still at large, and police and judiciary are investigating the injuries and working to arrest him. After Niloufar was declared brain dead, her family agreed to donate her two kidneys.

The price of gasoline outside the quota in Iran has increased to 100,000 rials per liter. This increase can generate less than 500 million dollars in additional annual revenue for the government. However, it will have limited impact on the fuel shortage.

The US, UK, France, and Germany have prepared a draft resolution to refer Iran's nuclear case to the UN Security Council. The draft has not yet been formally submitted to the IAEA Board of Governors, and negotiations are ongoing. The IAEA has warned that lack of inspector access to Iran's nuclear sites poses a proliferation risk that must be urgently addressed.

Oil prices have risen for the fourth consecutive day, nearing $100 per barrel. This increase followed the US announcement of destroying five oil tankers linked to the IRGC and a missile attack by the IRGC on a US base in Jordan. Analysts have suggested the possibility of Brent oil prices surging above $120.

Raf Chikoni, head of the Australian Parliament's intelligence committee, called the threats against Persian-speaking journalists by the IRGC unacceptable and emphasized their right to work freely. He urged global support for the Iranian people and the Iranian diaspora. Chikoni mentioned actions such as expelling Iranian diplomats and sanctioning individuals linked to the IRGC in Australia.

Richard Goldberg, an analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, wrote that the IRGC is in a losing position in its policy of escalating tensions. He added that each attack accelerates the organization's collapse. Additionally, the IRGC's tanker and air fleets are at risk of destruction and grounding.

A murder suspect in Tehran was sentenced to death. Additionally, three death penalty cases in Izeh, Masjed Soleyman, and Dezful ended in reconciliation. The victims' families' consent led to the suspects being spared from execution.

Ellen Burstyn, a 93-year-old American actress, received the Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement at the 83rd Venice Film Festival. In her speech, she highlighted the changing role of women in cinema and expressed hope for greater female presence. Report by Sadaf Baghbani, Iran International reporter.

Chuck Schumer, the Democratic minority leader in the US Senate, accused Donald Trump of dragging the US into an endless war. He said this war has caused soaring prices and endangered military forces abroad. Schumer emphasized that the war must end immediately.

Amir Mobarez Parasta stated that multiple networks in mental health and treatment have been established abroad to support families seeking justice. These supports can be provided through medical staff inside Iran and specialized networks abroad. The main goal is to ensure these families do not feel alone.

The price of some medicines in Iran has increased up to five times in one year. Patients' out-of-pocket expenses have reached about 80 percent. This situation has forced patients to make difficult choices.

Jamshid Barzegar said the increase in gasoline prices not only raises fuel costs but also leads to higher prices for goods and services and economic pressure on people. He added that the Islamic Republic has no plan to compensate for the gasoline deficit. Concerns about widespread protests have prevented further gasoline price increases.

The company Tanker Trackers reported that five Iranian oil tankers targeted by the US military on Tuesday have exported a total of 45 million barrels of crude oil and petroleum products since May 2019.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi stated that the goal of the Islamic Republic's attacks on American ships is to break sanctions and increase pressure on the Trump administration. These actions aim to force the US to withdraw from the region. Tensions in the area have escalated following these attacks.

Yemeni government forces have taken control of the Al-Atmah area in Al-Jawf province. A large-scale operation has started in Al-Bayda province, and clashes continue in the western coast and west of Taiz. After repelling recent Houthi ground attacks, government forces have launched a counterattack.
The US Central Command destroyed five oil tankers carrying Iranian crude oil. This action followed missile attacks by the IRGC on a US warship. No American personnel were harmed in these attacks.

The US Central Command announced that American forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday. This action followed two attempts by the IRGC to target a US warship. CENTCOM identified the tankers as part of a network financing the IRGC.

Recent reports have emerged about the theft of food items such as cheese, yogurt, cream, rice, and oil. Some accused individuals have no prior criminal record and have been arrested for theft for the first time. This issue raises concerns about the economic and living conditions of the people.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, stated that if Iran attempts to attack US Navy ships, Iranian oil tankers will be targeted. This statement reflects ongoing tensions between the two countries. Rubio directly threatened a retaliatory response.

The American company Anthropic reported identifying abusive activities using its AI models. The report mentions the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Mojahedin-e Khalq Organization. This has sparked widespread reactions among Iranian users.

Farzin Nadimi said the Houthi advance in Bab al-Mandab does not fundamentally change their ability to disrupt shipping. He considered the attack on the Saudi oil pipeline pump station a more significant development. This attack indicates the vulnerability of Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure.

The head of Iran's aviation organization protested the new US sanctions against the aviation industry. The Iranian Airlines Association stated that these sanctions will affect flight safety and the daily lives of millions of passengers. An interview was also conducted with Miad Maleki regarding the targeting of the sanctions.
IRNA reported hearing two explosions in Qeshm from the sea side. This news was released on Saturday evening. Local sources have not commented on the matter.

Workers at Pulur Sabz Zarand Wagon Factory and Omran Taradeh Company reported wage arrears. Workers at Saman Tile Factory in Borujerd also face job uncertainty and delayed wage and insurance claims. These issues have been reported in three different units.

Xi Jinping has officially announced his readiness to mediate between Tehran and Washington. This news was shared in the audio version of Titrawol with Niusha Saremi. The mediation topic has recently been raised.

Mehdi Mahdavi Azad stated that the Israeli army destroyed one of the largest military fortresses of the IRGC in the Ali al-Taher hills in southern Lebanon using about 1,100 tons of explosives. This operation is not limited to the destruction of a Hezbollah base but also weakens the reputation of the Islamic Republic and resistance groups among their supporters.

Channel 13 Israel reported that the Israeli army is preparing for the possibility of ballistic missile and drone attacks from Yemen amid escalating conflicts and developments in the Bab al-Mandab Strait. The main concern is the Houthi attacks on ships and their impact on global trade. The Israeli army is also examining the consequences of Yemen's developments on tensions between the US and the Islamic Republic in the Strait of Hormuz.
Abed Alizadeh, a citizen from Takab, was released today from Miandoab prison after posting bail.

During the seventh week of the Premier League, fans of Sanat Naft Abadan chanted against their coach Mohammad Nouri. The match against Chadormalu Ardakan was held at Takhti Abadan Stadium. Sanat Naft lost the game 2-1 and is at the bottom of the league table.

The Turkish Treasury Minister stated that payments for gas imported from Iran are not made directly to the Islamic Republic but are held in an account with strict regulations. Iran can only use this account to pay for authorized goods. Turkey cooperates with the US to combat money laundering and sanctions evasion.

Due to lack of workplace safety, two workers in Khondab and Bandar Mahshahr were involved in accidents. One worker died and another was injured. These incidents were reported to be caused by unsafe working conditions.

The appeals court reduced the prison sentence of Ali Mokhtari, a researcher and PhD student in public law at Beheshti University, to six months. Four months of this sentence have been suspended. He was previously sentenced to 18 months in prison.

Ali Cheldavi, a 13-year-old Arab child from Ahvaz, was arrested by the Intelligence Organization of the IRGC in the village of Oboudeh, Ahvaz. Mustafa Cheldavi and at least 10 other Sunni Arab citizens were also detained in this operation. Families are concerned about the detainees' condition, and the Karun Human Rights Organization has called for their release and clarification of their detention locations.

Ghassan Ashour stated that the Houthis have agreed not to attack US and other countries' ships except Saudi Arabia. He said they see this as an opportunity for military advancement. They may change their tactics in the future.

Abba Bush, Sweden's Deputy Prime Minister, called for increased financial and economic pressure on the Islamic Republic. He also emphasized that the Swedish government must protect Iranians residing in the country from threats by the Islamic Republic. He urged practical action to stop executions and political trials.

The US President emphasized strong control and a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz during a meeting with the Irish Prime Minister. He stated that CENTCOM forces stop an average of 25 vessels daily. CENTCOM announced that in the past 60 days, the routes of 100 commercial ships have been changed.

Shahram Khaledi stated that the Islamic Republic's actions in the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on regional energy infrastructure have led to a regional and international consensus against Tehran. He added that for years, the Islamic Republic has sought to impose its model on the Persian Gulf by disrupting regional security. This approach has faced opposition from regional countries and will ultimately fail.

Ricardo Sa Pinto, former coach of Esteghlal, criticized Ali Tajernia's interference in the team's lineup and player selections. He said Tajernia tried to impose a player named Ali Shojaei on him, which he refused. Sa Pinto also claimed that Saeed Fattahi was added to Esteghlal to manage relations with referees.

Real Madrid defeated Rayo Vallecano 4-1 in the fifth week of La Liga with a double from Kylian Mbappe and goals from Alvaro Carreras and Jude Bellingham. With their fourth win in five games, they are now level on points with Barcelona. Barcelona can retake the top spot if they win against Levante.

Masoud Pezeshkian reacted to the US economic pressures on Iran by calling for direct confrontation with US military forces. He questioned why the US wages war against civilian infrastructure and people's livelihoods. He also criticized depriving people of water, food, and medicine.

Mithaq Zareh said at the Venice Film Festival that government repression in Iran has caused despair and numbness among people. He emphasized that cinema has become a weapon against censorship. The film "A Little Light" tells the story of a doctor who decides to end his life after being arrested but finds new reasons to live.

Kambiz Tavana stated that increased Houthi influence over Bab al-Mandab could strengthen the Islamic Republic's regional leverage. He added that over 10 million barrels of oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz in the past seven days. No Iranian oil tankers were seen in this data.

Bijan Kian described the Houthi advance on the Red Sea coast as a tactical victory that could lead to a new coalition against the Islamic Republic. He also said the US is no longer willing to pay for regional security without strategic alignment with regional countries. Saudi Arabia and Gulf states must decide on their future relations with Tehran and Washington.

Hassan Mansour stated that the Islamic Republic's foreign exchange resources do not meet commercial needs. He warned that reduced imports could lead to shortages of essential goods. Additionally, the existing foreign exchange resources are not stable or reliable.

Laleh Marzban won the Best Actress award in the Horizons section at the Venice International Film Festival. The film, directed by Mohsen Gharaei, tells the story of a girl who wants to travel to Turkey but is confined at home by her father. Marzban dedicated her award to Iranian women and urged people not to lose hope.

Elena Rybakina defeated Aryna Sabalenka in the US Open final to win her third Grand Slam title. With this victory, she rose to the world number one ranking and ended Sabalenka's 20-match winning streak. Despite an ankle injury, Rybakina added the US Open trophy to her previous Australian Open and Wimbledon titles.

The Yemeni army targeted Houthi positions in Taiz with airstrikes. The Houthis attacked a military base in the Sharurah area of Saudi Arabia with drones and ballistic missiles. A projectile landing in Jazan, Saudi Arabia, injured two people and caused damage to civilian infrastructure.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. A ship was targeted by an unknown projectile while passing through the strait. The crew's condition and damages are currently unknown, and investigations are ongoing.

Esmail Kowsari and Vahid Ahmadi stated that no proposal regarding Iran's exit from the NPT has been submitted to the National Security Commission. Ahmadi emphasized that this issue should be reviewed by the commission, and the parliament has no sessions this week. Earlier, a representative announced the preparation of a proposal to exit the NPT.

On the early morning of Sunday, 22 Shahrivar, continuous gunfire was heard near police stations and military bases in the Bakhshan area of Saravan. The gunfire was one-sided, and the cause and type of weapon are unknown. This report came after a 9-hour clash between military forces and armed individuals affiliated with the People's Fighters Front.

The International Organization for Migration reported that at least 76,000 people have been displaced since July due to intensified clashes along Yemen's Red Sea coast. The number of displaced people has quadrupled in the past week, with 30,000 added in just a few days. Additionally, about 1,400 people entered Djibouti from Yemen within 24 hours.

Reduction of subsidies and fuel quotas in Iran has caused dissatisfaction and strikes among truck and taxi drivers. Long queues have formed at fuel stations. The government faces economic difficulties and pressures from sanctions.

Alexey Likhachov stated that 47 Rosatom specialists have returned to the Bushehr nuclear power plant, with plans to increase to 150. Scheduled maintenance for fuel assembly replacement will begin in mid-September. Construction of the second and third units and repairs of the first unit at Bushehr are also underway.

Kayhan newspaper wrote that the Islamic Republic should officially declare that in case of an attack on any Iranian tanker, all tankers within range will be targeted. This could lead to a reduction in operational tankers and a historic increase in oil prices. Kayhan emphasized the need for precise planning and use of military and economic capacities for aggressive deterrence.

Abbas Goudarzi, spokesperson of the Parliament's presidium, said that Iran's exit from the NPT and reconsideration of its nuclear doctrine would put the US in its place. He called negotiations with the US a strategic mistake that would weaken the resistance front. Goudarzi described the conflict between Iran and the US as intrinsic and fundamental.

Amir Teymouri, governor of Qeshm, announced that an Iranian commercial ship was hit around 5 AM on Sunday, September 12, near Hengam Island and the Shib Deraz coast of Qeshm Island. One person was killed and three were injured in the incident.

Hussein Mozaffari, the Friday prayer leader of Qazvin, described chastity and hijab as national and religious symbols and emphasized their preservation. He stated that society is influenced by the enemy's negative propaganda. Mozaffari stressed confronting the cultural conspiracies of the enemy.

Ahmad Nadari, a member of the parliament's presidium, stated that Iran's strategy in the Persian Gulf is based on ambiguity, deterrence, and strategic surprise. He added that there are surprises for the US that have not yet been unveiled. Nadari also emphasized that confrontation with the US is not only based on military power but also involves changing the opponent's calculations.

Mohammad Qaedi commented on the meeting of Arab foreign ministers in Muscat and the agreement between Iran and Oman on a joint route in the Strait of Hormuz. He said the meeting currently holds more symbolic importance. It may also pave the way for future security agreements.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated in an interview with India Today that Iran is currently not ready for direct talks with Donald Trump because their leader was killed. He added that building trust is necessary for negotiations. Pezeshkian also said Iran is not at war with Saudi Arabia and there is no reason for conflict among regional countries.

Ali Dadpay stated that the reduction in exports and limited access of the Islamic Republic to foreign currency resources decreases the ability to pay and transport goods. Using land routes cannot replace sea routes due to limited capacity and high transportation costs. Increased import costs and currency prices may intensify domestic inflation.

A group of Iranians gathered in Stockholm for the 255th consecutive day. The rally was held with slogans supporting Prince Reza Pahlavi. The aim was to attract the attention of the Swedish public and politicians to developments in Iran.

A group of housing project buyers from the Aryan Sazeh construction company protested in front of the Army Headquarters in Tehran on Saturday, September 12. They protested the delay in delivering projects such as Setin, Padefand, Afra, Gol Maryam, Pardis Shargh, and Abshar. These projects have been left unresolved for a long time.

Hossein Noushabadi criticized the IAEA Board of Governors resolution against Iran as lacking legal validity. He described the resolution as a political move by the US and three European countries to pressure the Islamic Republic. Noushabadi also called the Board of Governors a tool for countries violating international law principles.

Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, Fakhereh Zahedi, and Shima Sanaei, three Baha'i citizens, were released from Tircola prison in Sari on bail. Zahedi was released on September 6, Sanaei on September 7, and Manouchehrzadeh on September 9. A property bail worth two billion tomans was provided for each release.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said that the US and the Islamic Republic are trying to increase the cost of conflict for the other side in the Persian Gulf. He considers the continuation of the tanker war as the most likely short-term scenario. These remarks refer to the ongoing tensions in the region.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated in an interview with India Today that the Islamic Republic is not at war with Saudi Arabia. This statement came after a drone attack on the east-west pipeline in Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia and Iraq claimed the attack was launched from Iraqi territory.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of Iran International's editorial team, referred to Kayhan newspaper's note about targeting oil tankers in the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman. He said this view believes that land, people, and the country must be sacrificed for their ideals. Akbarin described these policies as continuing the path of destruction, poverty, and ruin for the country.

On the early morning of Sunday, 22 Shahrivar, the death sentences of six prisoners were carried out in the prisons of Iranshahr, Zabol, Zahedan, and Jiroft. These prisoners were sentenced for drug-related crimes. The executions were carried out in separate cases.

The president of Alzahra University reported difficulties in finding a contractor to provide student meals due to price increases. Contractors are unwilling to cooperate at last year's prices, requiring support. Financial problems and dormitory challenges were also mentioned.

Masoud Rangrazani was shot dead on the evening of Friday, January 9, 2026, in Islamshahr, Tehran. His family decorated the place where he was killed on the street. This video was released by Iran International.

Tuition fees in private schools have increased by up to 65 percent in some areas. Families face serious financial difficulties in covering educational and living expenses. There are also reports of plainclothes and Basij forces present in some regions.

Turkey and Azerbaijan are expanding their cooperation in electricity and renewable energy. The cooperation focuses on three main projects, including electricity connection via Nakhchivan, a green electricity corridor among four countries, and a power transmission line from the Black Sea to Europe. These projects could strengthen Turkey's position in regional energy transit.

Kylian Mbappe scored a penalty in Real Madrid's match against Rayo Vallecano, bringing his goal tally in the new La Liga season to 6. He is now only 8 goals away from Cristiano Ronaldo's record of 100 goals for Real Madrid. Mbappe has the opportunity to approach this historic record with upcoming matches.
